what: A kernel step cannot run a front-end query and see what it read: `Reads` hands out no world, and `blaze_query::db::capture_reads` captures nothing outside a running query, while a salsa memo that validates without running leaves no reads to capture at all. The body entries take the db through their identity read (`IdentityOf::get` returns the world) and take the trace from the item store, which keeps the last run's facts per (body, step, schema).
cost: most of a lane's design time; a second home for a run's trace (the store's trace table beside its record path)
cause: the front end's engine and the kernel are two engines over one computation: the kernel's step is defined by a salsa query whose reads only salsa sees
class: two engines memoizing one value, each blind to the other's reads
prevention: the kernel entry becomes the only lookup of a body's step (the query side reads the session's verified entry); then the record path and its blaze_record shapes are deleted
fix: owed: the query side through the kernel session (see the lane report)
